meta.title: Compact mode
meta.description: How the schedule adapts to the width it is given — its own width, not the viewport’s — and what changes when it does.

basics.intro: A schedule in a sidebar and a schedule filling a page are the same component at two widths. Compact mode is measured from the schedule’s own container with a ResizeObserver, never from the viewport and never from the user agent, so a narrow box inside a wide window is compact and a wide box inside a phone-sized iframe is not.
points: compact is 'auto' by default: true below compactBreakpoint, which is 900 pixels. A boolean forces it either way.
Compact tightens the cards, drops the timeline to one column, and narrows the pinned chips — 436 pixels at 900 and above, 360 between 600 and 899, and 90% of the width below that.
listOnlyBreakpoint is separate and stronger: below it the timeline is not offered at all.
On the server the component renders as not compact unless you pass a boolean, and the first measurement after hydration corrects it.
Nothing is removed in compact mode: the same items, the same headings, the same names, in fewer pixels.
Touch targets stay at least 24 by 24 pixels, which is what WCAG 2.2 asks for.
The measurement is of the container, so a reader who zooms to 200% gets the compact layout rather than a horizontally scrolling page.
compactBreakpoint and listOnlyBreakpoint set where the two thresholds are.
density is the other spacing dial and is independent of compact mode — see Theming.
useCompact gives the same measurement to markup of your own.
The thresholds are pixel widths, not container queries: a layout that changes shape without changing the schedule’s width does not change compact mode.
The pinned-chip widths are fixed at their three steps and cannot be set per application.
The first server-rendered frame cannot know the width, so a compact layout appears after hydration unless you pass the boolean yourself.
